title: getMoves picks the wrong 'previous' stint (start_year DESC NULLS LAST ignores end-year-only stints): wrong promoted/joined and wrong previous job on the home feed
detail: The previous-stint query orders by start_year DESC NULLS LAST. Many recent stints have only an end year (e.g. 'Randolph-Macon ?-2025'), so they sort below old dated stints. A coach who came from another program is then labeled 'promoted' with an old same-org GA job as 'previous'. Promotion is also decided by comparing short_name strings rather than org ids. 19 of 397 current-season moves show the wrong previous job and 4 flip kind. The orgIdBySlug map is dead code.
evidence: getMoves(1000) returns {kind:'promoted', who:'Matthew Szymanski', org:'Brockport', previous:{role:'Graduate Assistant / Linebackers Coach', orgShortName:'Brockport'}}, but his tenures are Brockport 2026-current, Brockport 2021-2021, Randolph-Macon ?-2025. Same for Daryl Jones (Southwestern 2016-22 picked over Taylor HS ?-2025). SQL comparing the current ordering with ORDER BY coalesce(end_year,start_year) DESC NULLS LAST: kind_flips=4, previous_changes=19.
fix: ORDER BY t.person_id, coalesce(t.end_year, t.start_year) DESC NULLS LAST, t.sort_order. Select o.id and compare org ids for 'promoted'. Remove orgIdBySlug.

verdict.reason:
The core bug reproduces, but the finding overstates its severity and part of its scope.

What I reproduced:
- I ran getMoves(1000) with tsx and --conditions react-server against the local coachnet DB. It returned 397 moves.
- It returns {kind:'promoted', who:'Matthew Szymanski', previous:{Graduate Assistant / Linebackers Coach, Brockport}}. His tenures are Brockport 2026-current (sort 0), Brockport 2021-2021 (sort 1) and Randolph-Macon ?-2025 as Co-DC (sort 2). He clearly came from Randolph-Macon, so 'promoted' is wrong.
- Daryl Jones is wrong in the same way. The query picks Southwestern 2016-2022 over Taylor High School ?-2025, so he shows as 'promoted' when he actually rejoined Southwestern from Taylor HS.
- Cause: `ORDER BY t.person_id, t.start_year DESC NULLS LAST` in /home/user/klonen_cli/web/src/lib/queries/feed.ts. Stints that have only an end year sort below old stints that have a start year. There is also no tie-break, so when several stints are all undated, DISTINCT ON picks one arbitrarily. For example, Christian Williams gets sort_order #8 instead of #1.
- I compared the current ordering with `coalesce(end_year, start_year) DESC NULLS LAST, sort_order`. The previous stint changes for 21 of 397 people (the finding said 19; ties are nondeterministic) and the kind flips for 4. That matches the finding closely.

Where the finding overstates:
1. No user sees this today. Nothing in the app renders getMoves or getFeed: /feed/page.tsx is a placeholder, and the only caller is scripts/smoke-queries.ts. The bug is real but latent. It will show up once the feed is built, because design/feature-briefs.json ('feed') says to build move cards from getMoves.
2. Only 2 of the 4 kind flips are clearly wrong (Szymanski and Daryl Jones). Javian Byrd has two 2025-2025 stints, so his case is ambiguous. The proposed fix would turn Felicia Teeter into 'promoted', from a John Carroll 2026-2026 women's flag football role, which is arguable either way.
3. Comparing short_name instead of org id has no effect today: no two organizations share a short_name. The unused orgIdBySlug map is just dead code.

Verdict: a real correctness bug in the query layer that will feed the planned home feed, with about 5% wrong previous jobs and some wrong promoted/joined labels. Severity is closer to moderate than major because nothing renders it yet.

title: getAlumni: DISTINCT ON picks undated stints (DESC puts NULLs first) and LIMIT cuts by person id, not recency
detail: The query uses ORDER BY people.id, tenures.end_year DESC. Postgres DESC sorts NULLs first, so for a person with both a dated and an undated past stint at the org, the undated one wins (80 person/org pairs affected). That person then sorts to the bottom of the JS re-sort. LIMIT is applied to rows ordered by people.id, so once an org has more than `limit` alumni (max today is 13; the default limit of 60 is exceeded at 10x), the kept alumni are the alphabetically first ids, not the most recent. The JS sort only reorders the arbitrary subset.
evidence: getAlumni('ncaa-46') (Baldwin Wallace) returns 'Andrew Cregan | Student-Coach null null' at the bottom; his BW stints include 'Assistant Coach; Quarterbacks Coach / Recruiting Coordinator 2022-2025'. getAlumni('ncaa-46', 5) returns brian-foos, andrew-cregan(null), andrew-danford(null), jim-dobney(null), matt-hanhold(null) and drops Rocky Zingale (2024-2025) and Noah Jackson (2020).
fix: Use a subquery: DISTINCT ON (person_id) ORDER BY person_id, coalesce(end_year,start_year) DESC NULLS LAST. Then in the outer query ORDER BY coalesce(end_year,start_year) DESC NULLS LAST, full_name LIMIT n.

verdict.reason: I reproduced it by calling the real getAlumni through tsx against the local coachnet database, and also ran the same SQL in psql. In web/src/lib/queries/orgs.ts the query uses DISTINCT ON (people.id) ORDER BY people.id, end_year DESC. Postgres sorts NULLs first under DESC, so a stint with no dates beats a dated one. For Baldwin Wallace (ncaa-46), Andrew Cregan has three stints there: a 2022-2025 non-player stint (Assistant Coach; Quarterbacks Coach / Recruiting Coordinator), an undated Student-Coach stint, and an undated player row that the query filters out. getAlumni returns 'Andrew Cregan | Student-Coach null null', and the JS re-sort then puts him last. So the page shows the wrong role and no seasons for someone who coached there last year. Across all person/org pairs, an undated stint wins over a dated one in 58 cases by my definition (the finding says 80, so the exact count depends on how 'dated' is defined, but there are dozens). The LIMIT part also reproduces: getAlumni('ncaa-46', 5) returns Foos, Cregan(null), Danford(null), Dobney(null) and Hanhold(null), and drops Rocky Zingale (2024-2025) and Noah Jackson (2020), because LIMIT is applied in people.id order before the JS sort runs. That part is latent with the default limit of 60, since the largest org has only 13 alumni. Two caveats lower the severity but don't refute the finding. First, nothing in the app calls getAlumni yet: the only caller is scripts/smoke-queries.ts, which just prints .length. Second, the planned /programs/[slug] page in design/feature-briefs.json names getAlumni as the source for its Alumni tab, so the wrong role and missing years will appear there as soon as that page is built. The bug is real; 'major' is arguably high given it isn't wired into the UI yet.

title: Profile 'seasons coached' and grouped experience claim continuous tenure across gaps and undated current roles (overstated career stats)
detail: stats.seasonsCoached = seasonCount(firstSeason, null, true), i.e. CURRENT_SEASON - first + 1. This ignores gaps and assumes continuity when the current role's start year is unknown (789 current roles are undated). groupExperience likewise sets startYear = min(start) and isCurrent = any(current), so separate stints plus an undated current role become 'YYYY–Present · N seasons'. This contradicts the 'never claim more than the source' principle; seasonRangeMulti already exists for multi-stint spans but is not used for the group or the stat.
evidence: getProfile('duane-russell') returns stats {stops:2, seasonsCoached:43} and the group 'Azusa Pacific 1984-now seasons=43'. Source tenures: Azusa current (start null), 1993-1995, 1984. SQL over all people: 1448 with dates, 322 where the naive count exceeds the years actually covered, 189 over by 3 or more, worst gap 39 (duane-russell 43 vs 4, claud-allaire 40 vs 2).
fix: Compute seasonsCoached as the count of distinct covered years (merge spans as seasonRangeMulti does, and count an undated current role as 1 season, not a span). In groupExperience, keep isCurrent but don't extend an old start year into 'Present' unless the current role's own start year links them. Use seasonRangeMulti(g.roles) for g.seasons.

verdict.reason:
The numbers reproduce exactly, and the grouping half is a real spec violation. Two caveats: the bug is latent, and the stat half is weaker.

What I reproduced: I ran getProfile through tsx against the local Postgres.
- duane-russell returns stats {stops:2, seasonsCoached:43, treeSize:1}. The Azusa Pacific group comes out as 1984–Present, 43 seasons, built from tenures (current, no start year), 1993–1995 and 1984.
- seasonRangeMulti on the same roles gives "1984, 1993–1995 / 4 seasons · 2 stints".
- claud-allaire returns 40 seasons coached.
- I re-ran the scan over the whole dataset. It found 319 people whose start-to-now count exceeds the years their dated stints cover, close to the finding's 322.

Why the grouping half is a real bug: groupExperience takes min(start) through Present across consecutive same-org roles, so non-contiguous stints become one continuous span. DESIGN.md §6.1 says non-contiguous stints at one program must show as "2003, 2006–2009 / 5 seasons · 2 stints". Its fixed-issues table (#32) explicitly rejects "2003–2009 · 5 seasons" because it "implied seven straight years". The source evidence contradicts the output in clear cases:
- bo-beatty's bio says "He returned for coaching stints in 2006–07 and again in 2009-10". The group comes out as "Azusa Pacific 1995–Present · 32 seasons" instead of 7 seasons in 3 stints.
- bill-giovino-88's bio says "began his second stint coaching at LVC in 2014". The group comes out as "1995–Present · 32" instead of "1995–1996, 2014–Present · 15 seasons · 2 stints".
- adam-eichhorn: "2007–Present · 20" instead of "2007–2008, 2017–Present · 12".

Caveats:
1. Latent. Nothing renders getProfile yet. There is no /in/[slug] route in src/app or in the .next build, and the only caller is scripts/smoke-queries.ts. So no user sees "43 seasons" today. design/feature-briefs.json does tell the profile page to build on getProfile, and ExperienceGroup.startYear/endYear/seasons are exposed for display, so the defect will reach users when that page ships. "Major" overstates it today.
2. The seasonsCoached half is debatable. Counting from the first known season to now is a defensible definition. The reference design's "First season 2002 / 25 seasons" is consistent with it. Many people flagged have undated stints that may fill the gaps; claud-allaire, for example, has 12 stops and 9 undated stints. The proposed fix (count only covered years, an undated current role = 1) would badly undercount, giving claud-allaire 3 seasons. Still, 68 people are over by 3 or more with no undated past stints at all (e.g. bo-beatty 32 vs 8), and those do overclaim.

Verdict: real. The grouping logic should use merged spans (seasonRangeMulti-style) for both the range and the count. The stat change needs care to avoid undercounting.

title: Seeded hiring pipeline puts 9 real coaches (one entire real staff) into a fake DC search at a real program, with 'offer' and 'interview' stages and a made-up reference note
detail: The candidates are people.filter(coordinator|position_coach).slice(0,9). Because of the data order, all 9 are Concordia (WI)'s current staff. They are placed in Morgan Ellis's (fictional AD) 'Defensive Coordinator search' at the real Pacific University: Zak DeWindt at 'offer', Ashar Thomas at 'interview' with the note 'Strong references from the head coach.' Pacific has a real incumbent DC (John Bates). Separately, sample 'Defensive Coordinator' jobs were seeded at Allegheny and Bethany, whose program pages list real incumbent DCs. These are fabricated statements about identifiable people's job searches and employment. The seed comment promises not to alter real records, but these attached records do the equivalent.
evidence: psql: shortlist_entries joined to people gives 9 rows, all short_name 'Concordia (WI)', stages sourced/contacted/interview/offer, note 'Strong references from the head coach.' on Ashar Thomas. People at ncaa-2751 include 'John Bates | Defensive Coordinator/Linebackers'. jobs vs incumbents: Allegheny DC job vs Matt Hanhold (Defensive Coordinator), Bethany DC job vs Josh Perry.
fix: Use clearly fictional candidates (isDemo people with invented names) for the pipeline, or at least no stages or notes implying offers or references. Don't seed sample openings for roles that a real person in the dataset currently holds at that program (or use fictional programs).

verdict.reason:
The finding reproduces, with a few overstatements and one caveat about when it becomes visible.

**What I confirmed:**
- In /home/user/klonen_cli/web/scripts/seed.ts, lines 129-132 take the first 9 people with roleGroup coordinator or position_coach who are not at Pacific. I replayed this against data/people.json and checked the live DB (coachnet, as user coach). It gives Curran White, Joseph Federico, Jeff Merritt, Nicholas Erling, Tristan Simpson-King, Ashar Thomas, Richie Dehnel, Zak DeWindt and Whitney Dobson, all at Concordia (WI).
- Every one of them has isDemo=false and a sourceUrl on cuwfalcons.com, so they are real, identifiable coaches. There are no isDemo people in the dataset at all.
- The DB shows Zak DeWindt at stage 'offer', Ashar Thomas and Richie Dehnel at 'interview', and the made-up note "Strong references from the head coach." on Ashar Thomas.
- The shortlist is "Defensive Coordinator search", owned by Morgan Ellis (fictional, isDemo) at Pacific (OR), ncaa-2751. Pacific's real incumbent DC, John Bates ("Defensive Coordinator/Linebackers"), is in the dataset.
- I replayed rng(2026): sample "Defensive Coordinator" jobs land at Allegheny (incumbent Matt Hanhold), Bethany (incumbent Josh Perry) and Guilford. The DB matches. The Allegheny job is also jobRows[0], which feeds the demo coach's job_match notification.
- This breaks the project's own rules. docs/DESIGN.md says "Never generate prose about a real person" and "Demo stats are never presented as facts about a real person's career". Proposal c-product says "we will not put a job-search signal in a real person's mouth".

**Overstatements and mitigations:**
- "One entire real staff" is wrong: it is 9 of Concordia (WI)'s 13 listed staff. The head coach and 3 assistants are left out.
- The pipeline page (web/src/app/employers/pipeline/page.tsx) is still a placeholder. No code in src reads shortlist entries yet, so nothing is rendered today. The harm is latent, but close: design/feature-briefs.json tells the next feature pass to render this board "seeded with 9 candidates", showing name, real program and note. Anyone can open it by picking the demo athletic director account.
- The sample-job half is weaker. Those listings carry the "Sample listing" chip and the text "This is a sample listing created for the demo. It is not a real opening." That reduces, but does not remove, the suggestion that a named real DC's job is open.

**Verdict:** The core problem is real and reproducible. The seed attaches recruiting stages (offer, interview) and a fabricated reference note to real, named coaches. "Major" is defensible because of the project's stated principles, even though nothing shows in the UI yet.

title: Conference footnote markers ('NACC[g]') split conferences in facets, filters, org search and carousel
detail: The markers are stripped only at display time (conferenceShort). facetOptions and listConferences return both 'NACC' and 'NACC[g]', which render as two identical 'NACC' options. Filtering on conference='NACC' (searchPeople, listJobs) excludes Concordia (WI). searchOrgs' exact-conference match misses it. getCarouselStats groups the two separately. Affects NACC, NJAC and SAA.
evidence: facetOptions() conferences include ['NACC','NACC[g]','NJAC','NJAC[r]','SAA','SAA[m]'], displayed as NACC, NACC, NJAC, NJAC, SAA, SAA. searchOrgs('nacc') returns 8 orgs without Concordia (WI) (NACC[g]). searchPeople({conference:'NACC'}).total=77 vs NACC[g]=13.
fix: Clean conference_abbr in the data or seed (regexp_replace '\[[^\]]*\]'), or compare and group on the cleaned expression in SQL.

verdict.reason:
The finding reproduces against the local coachnet database, and the claimed numbers match exactly. The organizations table has conference_abbr values 'NACC[g]' (Concordia (WI)), 'NJAC[r]' (Vermont State Castleton) and 'SAA[m]' (Millsaps, Southwestern), alongside the plain 'NACC', 'NJAC' and 'SAA'.

I ran the real query functions with tsx:
- facetOptions().conferences and listConferences() both contain ['NACC','NACC[g]','NJAC','NJAC[r]','SAA','SAA[m]']. Passed through conferenceShort, these become NACC, NACC, NJAC, NJAC, SAA, SAA.
- searchOrgs('nacc') returns 8 orgs and Concordia (WI) is not among them.
- searchPeople({conference:'NACC'}).total is 77, and NACC[g] is 13. Those 13 coaches can never be reached through the 'NACC' filter. listJobs uses the same eq() comparison (jobs.ts:13).
- getCarouselStats groups by the raw abbreviation (feed.ts:151).

format.ts says the bracket suffix is a footnote marker left over from source tables, which confirms 'NACC[g]' means 'NACC'. So this is a data-normalisation bug, not two real conferences.

Caveats on impact, which keep it minor:
- The /search, /jobs and feed pages are still placeholders. facetOptions, listConferences, searchPeople, listJobs and getCarouselStats are only called from scripts/smoke-queries.ts, so the duplicate dropdown options and filter exclusions are not visible in the UI yet. They are latent in the query layer that those features will use.
- With the cleaned grouping, the carousel's current top 5 (PAC 39, MAC 30, NCAC 25, MWC 21, Centennial 19) does not change, so that symptom is theoretical today.
- One symptom is live now: /api/typeahead calls searchOrgs(term, 4). typeahead('nacc') returns Aurora, Benedictine, Concordia (IL), Eureka. With a cleaned comparison, Concordia (WI) would rank 4th alphabetically among exact conference matches and would appear instead of Eureka.

The bug is real, correctly described and correctly rated minor. Current user-facing impact is limited to the typeahead.

title: searchPeople silently drops workedAt/workedUnder filters for an unknown slug and returns the whole database
detail: When the org or mentor slug isn't found, the `if (org)` / `if (mentor)` guards skip adding the predicate, so a stale or typo'd 'Worked under X' link shows all coaches as if they matched.
fix: If the slug doesn't resolve, return {results:[], total:0} (or push sql`false`).

verdict.reason:
The finding reproduces exactly. I ran searchPeople against the seeded local Postgres using tsx with --conditions=react-server. Results: no filter gives total=2178. workedUnder:'does-not-exist' also gives 2178, while workedUnder:'bill-khayat' gives 16. workedAt:'nope' gives 2178 and workedAt:'brevard' gives 19.

The cause is in /home/user/klonen_cli/web/src/lib/queries/search.ts, lines 39-54. The EXISTS predicate is only pushed inside `if (org)` and `if (mentor)`. When the slug doesn't resolve, the filter is dropped without any signal. For workedAt, context comes back as null, and the result gives no indication that a filter was ignored.

This is a real defect, not a design choice. Other filters with unknown values return nothing: division:'bogus' gives 0 and state:'ZZ' gives 0. Only these two slug filters fail open and return the whole database.

Caveat on impact: right now nothing calls searchPeople except web/scripts/smoke-queries.ts, and /search (src/app/search/page.tsx) is still a placeholder. So no user can hit this today. It is a latent bug in the query function that docs/ARCHITECTURE.md names as the backend for `/search?workedAt=&workedUnder=`. Once that route is built, a stale or hand-edited link would show every coach as matching. The "minor" severity is appropriate.

title: initials() produces wrong avatar initials for ~106 names with suffixes or class years
detail: It takes the last whitespace token as the surname, so class-year and generational suffixes are used as initials. 106 people in the DB end with Jr./Sr./II/III or 'YY.
evidence: initials("Dan Galante '87") returns "D'"; initials('Gerald Harrison Jr.') returns 'GJ'; initials('Bob Smith III') returns 'BI'. psql count of names matching the suffix regex = 106 (e.g. "Dr. Karl Liedtka '91", 'Chris Rutledge, Jr.').
fix: Strip trailing tokens matching /^('\d{2}|Jr\.?|Sr\.?|I{2,3}|IV|V|DPT)$/i, commas, and a leading 'Dr.' before taking the first and last tokens.

verdict.reason:
The finding reproduces. I ran a copy of initials() from web/src/lib/format.ts in node. It returns "D'" for "Dan Galante '87", "GJ" for "Gerald Harrison Jr.", "BI" for "Bob Smith III", "D'" for "Dr. Karl Liedtka '91" and "CJ" for "Chris Rutledge, Jr.". The function strips parentheses and then takes the first letter of the first and last whitespace tokens, so a class year or generational suffix becomes the second initial.

The count also holds. Against the local coachnet DB, people.full_name ~* '(''\d{2}|\mJr\.?|\mSr\.?|\mI{2,3}|\mIV)\s*$' matches exactly 106 of 2178 rows (about 4.9%). Examples include "AJ Glines '18, DPT '21", "Jason Lebeau '10/'16" and "LCDR Paul Puddington '16" (that last one also has a rank prefix).

Users do see it. The global search typeahead (app/api/typeahead/route.ts maps name: p.fullName, and TypeaheadPanel.tsx renders <Avatar name={o.name}>) shows these raw full names in Avatar, which calls initials(name) whenever there is no photo. Avatars on wrong rows show strings like "D'", "J'" or "BI". The existing tests only cover simple names.

Impact is small: wrong letters in an aria-hidden 24px avatar, with no data or logic effect. But it is plainly visible on about 5% of people, so I rate it a real minor bug, not a negligible one.
